speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San
text: asked the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth with the evolving COVID-19 situation (a) whether Singapore will heighten measures to ensure safety and welfare of participants in the Singapore International Festival of Arts (SIFA) 2020; (b) how will the COVID-19 situation affect the attendance of SIFA 2020 events; and (c) whether there are proposed plans to give further support to the arts community for this annual festival.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth)
text: NAC will work with AHL towards an exciting SIFA line-up in 2021.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth)
text: These could include webcasts, behind-the-scenes profiling, as well as digital conversations.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth)
text: I encourage the arts community to likewise explore digital-based presentations of their work, so that they can continue to engage existing audiences, and develop new audiences, even in the current situation.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth)
text: For example, the Singapore Chinese Orchestra has made available its "Dabao" digital concert series on Facebook.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth)
text: NAC is also engaging potential partners to explore ways to support the online presentation of artworks and productions by the arts community.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth)
text: I urge those who have capability in this area to support others who may not have the same experience and proficiency.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth)
text: MOF has given notice to table a Supplementary Supply Bill to give greater support to Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth)
text: NAC is monitoring the situation closely and welcomes suggestions from our arts community on how we can address the challenges brought about by the COVID-19 situation together.

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: One, in view of the cancellation of SIFA, are there any plans to turn this into a #SGUnited Digital Arts Festival, by making the arts accessible and available?

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: Two, whether more can be done to engage our local freelance artists and arts groups for the future SIFAs and for other art events to make the local artists and arts companies as the preferred choice for programming?

speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
text: Three, can SIFA also explore to work with the Giving.sg to encourage online giving to the arts, such as turning the refund of tickets into donation and that could also apply to other arts companies?

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: On presenting a digital format of SIFA 2020, as mentioned in my reply, the Festival Director is already in talks with the local production companies on how they could re-purpose or adapt their works planned for this SIFA into a digital format, but probably in different versions because performing arts is best enjoyed live, in front of you on stage, in a live situation, with live audiences.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: So, we would have to respect how they would think their works can be best presented and we do encourage them to explore innovative ways, including digital means, to showcase their talents and their works to the audiences.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: In terms of local talents involved in SIFA, that has been the mandate and vision of SIFA over the years.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: As to encouraging audiences who have bought tickets for SIFA to donate the ticket refunds to the arts, yes, I think that would be a good suggestion that AHL could perhaps look at in terms of a platform.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: But giving to Giving.sg is already a platform for all to donate to a cause or a particular beneficiary of their choice.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: They would already be commissioned works and therefore, AHL – the organiser of SIFA – would already be working with them on their costs.
